searches.reason: Develop controlled sequence interventions that test whether recommendations depend on recent repeated interests or incidental older interactions. Use training-history prefixes, matched replacements, truncation, and order perturbations; measure rank changes against popularity controls. This could connect failures to sequence encoding and recency weighting without treating sensitivity as proof of correctness.

searches.reason: Build evidence-grounded probes for unsupported prerequisites, duplication, and useful complements using only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Investigate explicit evidence requirements and abstention when compatibility or purchase intent cannot be established. Calibrate rejection reasons and immediate-choice versus merely-plausible judgments against the twenty users’ feedback, without assuming unobserved traits.
searches.query: recommendation diagnostic evaluation grounded user feedback product compatibility prerequisites complement substitute redundancy uncertainty abstention textual metadata 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Establish whether diagnostic signals predict actionable ranking improvements. Compare fixed sampled-candidate and full-catalog unseen-item diagnostics on training-only temporal holdouts, quantify uncertainty across four datasets, and validate selected signals through targeted component ablations. Keep the pinned validation HR@10 protocol unchanged and distinguish training diagnostics from selection metrics.
